title: Tankless On-Demand Water Heater Install: Concentric Venting, Recirculation, and Test (Ask This Old House)

locations.name: Milwaukee, Wisconsin (probable)
locations.basis: Transcript references Milwaukee and Cream City brick; host thanks audience for coming to Milwaukee, suggesting the shoot location.

summary: This Old House hosts replace a 40-gallon tank heater in a Milwaukee-area home with a wall-mounted on-demand unit. The episode covers historical venting practices, the rationale for switching to a tankless system, and a complete installation sequence: upgrading gas supply, installing concentric venting, routing cold and hot water lines, adding an expansion tank and condensate drain, and connecting a recirculation pump with a crossover valve to reduce water waste. The installer explains the unit’s heat-exchanger design (primary and secondary exchangers), safety features (TPR valve, purge), and controls, and demonstrates immediate hot water at a faucet. The program emphasizes space savings, long-term durability (stainless steel and copper vs glass-lined tanks), and a claimed energy savings around 30%, while noting design considerations for homes with multiple bathrooms and distant fixtures.
topics: Material durability: stainless steel and copper vs glass-lined steel
Fixture placement considerations for multi-bath homes
Heritage brick context (Cream City brick) and architectural notes

sections.title: Ventilation history and basement context
concepts: How modern high-efficiency systems change venting requirements
sections.description: The host discusses a basement with an aging water heater and potential venting issues. A mini history lesson contrasts old coal-fired furnace venting with modern high-efficiency equipment, explaining why the existing chimney and flue can rot from the inside while newer equipment vents directly outside.

sections.title: What is an on-demand water heater?
concepts: Global usage (common in Europe/Asia) vs. US market share
sections.description: The installer introduces the on-demand unit as a wall-hung, instantaneous water heater, noting it heats water only when a faucet is opened, unlike a tank-type heater that runs continuously.

sections.title: How the on-demand heater works (heat exchangers)
concepts: Heat transfer to water via copper piping
sections.description: A step-by-step walkthrough of the internal gas burner, primary exchanger, secondary exchanger, and condensate handling, illustrating how heat is extracted and transferred to hot water with multiple stages.

sections.title: Why switch to tankless: durability and efficiency
concepts: Lifetime materials (stainless steel, copper) vs glass-lined tanks
sections.description: The host contrasts the durability and long-term operating costs of a tankless unit with a traditional tank, including a claimed energy reduction and the ability to supply continuous hot water.

sections.title: Site preparation and old unit removal
sections.description: The crew drains the existing tank and prepares the space for the wall-mounted unit, setting the stage for the new installation.

sections.title: Installation details: gas, venting, water, expansion, relief
concepts: One-inch gas line run from meter
Concentric (direct) vent for intake and exhaust
sections.description: Key installation steps including routing a larger gas feed, nesting intake/exhaust in a concentric pipe, adding an expansion tank, connecting the cold water line, and installing safety and condensate connections.

sections.title: Controls and commissioning
sections.description: The technician demonstrates how to set the unit’s temperature and explains basic commissioning tasks, including safety considerations and initialization checks.

sections.title: Upstairs recirculation concept and valve
concepts: Reducing wait time for hot water at distant fixtures
sections.description: A detailed exploration of mitigating the ‘cold water sandwich’ with a bronze recirculation pump and a crossover valve, including how the valve allows heat to loop back to the farthest fixture and keeps hot water readily available at the faucet.

sections.title: Test and demonstration of hot water performance
concepts: Comparative behavior with tankless vs tank
sections.description: The tester asserts the hot water heats quickly when the faucet is opened, demonstrating the unit’s performance and addressing common concerns about waiting for hot water in a multi-bath home.

sections.title: Final takeaways and considerations
concepts: Suitability for homes with two bathrooms
sections.description: Closing reflections discuss how the system fits a home with two bathrooms, balancing hot-water availability with energy use, and noting the importance of advanced controls to optimize performance.

featured_techniques.technique: On-demand water heater operation triggered by faucet use
Gas line sizing and purging during installation
Expansion tank installation and cold-water feed connection

Recirculation pump with crossover valve to eliminate hot-water delay
Test demonstration: achieved hot water at faucet immediately after activation
Official note on energy efficiency and durability (30% energy savings claim; stainless/copper vs glass-lined)
